page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The compute subsystem contains 8 dedicated physical cores from the AWS Neoverse-N1 processor family clocked at 2.5 GHz, operating with one thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration bundles 1875 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network interface, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the average performance tier for general multi-threaded compute and operational database workloads. In CPU benchmarks, the system achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 12132.09 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 5360.0. Cache-read bandwidth measured 472.81 GB/sec, while uncached 256MB read and write memory bandwidth reached 116.33 GB/sec and 55.8 GB/sec respectively. Operational data processing delivered 9.8 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a score of 5224.61 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, compression and vector tasks yielded lower percentiles, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression registering 7.19 GB/sec and PassMark encryption scoring 1086.33.

The primary efficiency advantage of the i4g.2xlarge lies in its dense ratio of NVMe storage and system memory to dedicated ARM vCPUs, which avoids the latency overhead associated with network-attached storage volumes. A measurable architectural tradeoff is moderate single-thread execution speed and the absence of specialized x86 instruction sets, which limits throughput on heavy compression tasks and machine learning prompt processing. The instance profile is suited for transactional databases, distributed key-value datastores, in-memory caching layers, search index hosts, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 8 dedicated Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, 64.0 GB of system memory, and an integrated 1875 GB NVMe SSD volume. Baseline networking is provisioned at 5 Gbps. Benchmark metrics indicate mid-range execution for multi-threaded computational workloads and data services, demonstrated by 9.8 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 5224.61 on PassMark database testing. In contrast, single-thread vector and decompression capabilities evaluate lower, as seen in bzip3 and encryption results. By combining local NVMe media with an 8.0 GB per-core memory configuration, the instance delivers high local data density, making it technically suited for transactional database engines, NoSQL datastores, search indexing nodes, and caching environments.
